explanation.concept: Organizations centralizes billing and policy management across many accounts
explanation.correct: AWS Organizations lets a company centrally manage billing (via consolidated billing) and enforce security/compliance policies (via Service Control Policies) across all member accounts from one management account.

distractors.B: Trusted Advisor gives account-level best-practice checks (cost, performance, security, limits) for a single account; it doesn't manage other accounts.
distractors.C: IAM User Groups organize users and permissions within one account; they can't manage billing or policy across separate AWS accounts.
distractors.D: AWS Config tracks and evaluates resource configuration compliance within an account; it has no multi-account billing or policy management role.

explanation.concept: Object storage (S3) vs block storage (EBS/Instance Store) vs file storage (EFS)
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 stores data as objects (data plus metadata plus key) in buckets, accessed over HTTP(S) — the definition of object-level storage in AWS.

distractors.A: Amazon EBS provides block storage volumes attached to a single EC2 instance, not object storage.
distractors.B: Instance Store is temporary block storage physically attached to the host, lost when the instance stops.
distractors.C: Amazon EFS provides file-level storage accessed via the NFS protocol, shared across multiple instances.

explanation.concept: Auto Scaling matches compute capacity to demand automatically
explanation.correct: AWS Auto Scaling monitors demand and automatically adds or removes EC2 instances to keep capacity matched to load, avoiding paying for idle, underutilized resources.

distractors.A: Elastic Load Balancer distributes incoming traffic across existing instances; it doesn't add or remove capacity itself.
distractors.B: AWS Budgets tracks and alerts on spend against a budget; it doesn't change compute capacity.
distractors.D: Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes historical spending; it's a reporting tool, not a capacity-management feature.

explanation.concept: Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between tiers as access patterns change
explanation.correct: S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors access patterns and automatically moves objects between frequent- and infrequent-access tiers, which is ideal when you don't know or can't predict how often data will be accessed.

distractors.B: Glacier Flexible Retrieval is for archival data accessed rarely, with retrieval delays — not for data with unknown access frequency.
distractors.C: S3 Standard is for frequently accessed data; choosing it assumes a known, high access pattern.
distractors.D: Standard-Infrequent Access assumes you already know access will be infrequent, which contradicts 'unpredictable'.

explanation.concept: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/NoSQL database
explanation.correct: Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database that stores data as key-value pairs (and documents), designed for exactly this data model.

distractors.B: Aurora is a relational (SQL) database compatible with MySQL/PostgreSQL, not key-value.
distractors.C: Redshift is a relational data warehouse for analytics, using SQL and columnar storage.
distractors.D: RDS provisions relational databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, etc.); it uses tables and SQL, not key-value structures.

explanation.concept: On-Demand pricing has no upfront cost, only a pay-as-you-go rate
explanation.correct: There is no start-up fee for On-Demand instances — you simply pay the hourly (or per-second, for Linux) rate for what you use, with no upfront commitment. This statement is false, which is why it's the answer.

distractors.B: True: On-Demand follows the pay-as-you-go model, which is why it is not the incorrect statement.
distractors.C: True: On-Demand requires no long-term contract or upfront payment, unlike Reserved Instances.
distractors.D: True: On-Demand Linux instances are billed per second (minimum 60 seconds), based on an hourly rate.

explanation.concept: Trusted Advisor checks configuration best practices; Inspector scans for vulnerabilities
explanation.correct: AWS Trusted Advisor reviews the account against security best-practice checks (like open ports or public S3 buckets), and Amazon Inspector automatically scans EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure — together covering proper security settings.

distractors.C: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub messaging service; it plays no role in checking security configuration.
distractors.D: Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics, logs, and alarms for operational performance, not security posture assessment.
distractors.E: There is no AWS offering called 'Concierge Support Team' for security review — Concierge is a billing-focused role under Enterprise Support.

explanation.concept: MFA adds a second authentication factor beyond username/password
explanation.correct: AWS Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires a second factor — a code from a hardware or virtual device — in addition to the username and password, raising the security bar above single-factor login.

distractors.A: 'Encrypted keys' isn't a named AWS authentication feature; it doesn't describe an added login factor.
distractors.B: Email verification isn't AWS's standard extra authentication mechanism for console or API sign-in.
distractors.C: AWS KMS manages encryption keys for data protection; it is unrelated to user sign-in authentication.

explanation.concept: Infrastructure Event Management is the Enterprise-plan service for launch and scaling events
explanation.correct: Infrastructure Event Management (IEM) is an Enterprise Support engagement where AWS architects review and provide guidance for planned events such as a product launch expecting a traffic surge.

distractors.A: The AWS Knowledge Center is a library of articles and FAQs, not a proactive architectural engagement.
distractors.B: The AWS Health Dashboard reports on service health and events affecting your account, not scaling guidance for a launch.
distractors.D: AWS Support Concierge handles billing and account questions, not architectural or scaling guidance.

explanation.concept: RDS offloads undifferentiated database administration
explanation.correct: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service that handles provisioning, patching, backups, and disaster-recovery setup, freeing the DBA to focus on schema design and performance rather than infrastructure upkeep.

distractors.B: Redshift is a managed data warehouse for analytics, not a general-purpose relational OLTP replacement for MySQL.
distractors.C: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database; migrating a MySQL workload there means redesigning the data model, not just offloading maintenance.
distractors.D: CloudWatch is a monitoring service; it doesn't perform database backups, patching, or DR.

explanation.concept: Automation is a core AWS design principle that reduces friction for change
explanation.correct: Automating wherever possible (infrastructure as code, automated deployments) makes it cheap and safe to experiment with and change your architecture, which is a foundational AWS Well-Architected design principle.

distractors.A: The cloud specifically enables you to change your design later; treating the initial architecture as fixed contradicts cloud design principles.
distractors.B: Reservations are a production cost-optimization tool; using them for a test environment (which should scale down or off) wastes money.
distractors.D: Provisioning large fixed capacity 'just in case' is the traditional data-center approach — the cloud principle is to scale dynamically instead.

explanation.concept: AWS pre-authorizes penetration testing on a defined list of services
explanation.correct: Under the AWS Acceptable Use Policy, customers may perform penetration testing on their own instances and resources for a set of permitted services without needing prior AWS authorization, as long as they stay within the policy's rules.

distractors.A: Penetration testing is allowed for permitted services — it's not banned outright.
distractors.B: AWS doesn't automatically pen test your infrastructure for you; testing is something the customer initiates.
distractors.D: Customers can test their own resources built on AWS-managed services (within policy), not only services AWS itself manages.

explanation.concept: SQS decouples components with a durable message queue
explanation.correct: Amazon SQS is a managed message-queuing service that durably stores messages between producers and consumers, so if a component fails, queued messages are retained and processed once it recovers.

distractors.B: Amazon SES sends and receives email; it isn't a queuing mechanism for inter-component messages.
distractors.C: AWS Direct Connect is a dedicated network link into AWS; it doesn't durably queue or protect application messages.
distractors.D: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact-center service, unrelated to inter-component message durability.

explanation.concept: Design-for-failure means redundancy (AZs) plus automatic traffic rerouting (load balancing)
explanation.correct: Multiple Availability Zones (B) give physically independent, redundant infrastructure so a single facility failure doesn't take down the workload, and Elastic Load Balancing (C) automatically routes traffic away from unhealthy resources — together they implement 'design for failure'.

distractors.A: MFA is a security/authentication control, not a resilience mechanism against component failure.
distractors.D: Penetration testing finds security weaknesses; it doesn't make an architecture resilient to failure.
distractors.E: Vertical scaling makes one resource bigger, creating a single point of failure rather than removing it.

explanation.concept: VPC is your logically isolated virtual network in AWS
explanation.correct: Amazon VPC lets you provision a logically isolated virtual network dedicated to your account, where you control IP ranges, subnets, route tables, and gateways.

distractors.A: AWS VPN provides an encrypted connection into your network; it doesn't itself define your dedicated virtual network.
distractors.B: Subnets are subdivisions within a VPC, not a standalone dedicated-network service.
distractors.C: Dedicated Hosts are physical EC2 servers dedicated to your account, unrelated to network isolation.

explanation.concept: Customer owns data-in-transit protection and guest-level software
explanation.correct: Protecting the confidentiality of data in transit (B) and patching applications installed on EC2 (E) are customer responsibilities — the customer controls how data is encrypted in their application and must maintain the software they install on top of the OS.

distractors.A: Managing environmental events of AWS data centers is AWS's responsibility (security 'of' the cloud).
distractors.C: Controlling physical access to AWS Regions and data centers is exclusively AWS's job.
distractors.D: Ensuring the underlying EC2 host is configured properly is part of AWS's infrastructure responsibility, not the customer's.

explanation.concept: EC2 and Lambda are compute; VPC/CloudWatch/S3 are not
explanation.correct: Amazon EC2 (D) provides virtual server compute capacity, and AWS Lambda (E) runs code in a serverless compute model — both are compute resources.

distractors.A: Amazon VPC is networking, defining the virtual network your resources live in — not compute.
distractors.B: Amazon CloudWatch is a monitoring and observability service, not something that runs your workload.
distractors.C: Amazon S3 is object storage; it stores data, it doesn't execute code.

explanation.concept: S3 is the default choice for durable object storage of media files
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 is purpose-built object storage for files like photos and videos, offering high durability, virtually unlimited scale, and direct HTTP access — the standard recommendation for this use case.

distractors.A: EBS is block storage attached to a single EC2 instance; it isn't designed for shareable, internet-accessible media storage.
distractors.B: SQS is a message queue, not a storage service for binary files.
distractors.D: Instance store is temporary, host-attached storage that's lost when the instance stops — unsuitable for durable media.

explanation.concept: Access keys are the programmatic equivalent of a console username/password
explanation.correct: Access Keys (an access key ID and secret access key) authenticate programmatic requests to AWS APIs, CLI, and SDKs, serving the same authentication role that a username and password serve for console sign-in.

distractors.A: 'Instance Password' isn't a real AWS credential type.
distractors.B: Key pairs are used to SSH into EC2 instances, not to authenticate general AWS API calls.
distractors.D: MFA is a second factor added on top of primary credentials, not a replacement for username and password.

explanation.concept: ElastiCache is a managed in-memory data store for caching
explanation.correct: Amazon ElastiCache provides managed in-memory caching (Redis or Memcached engines), which dramatically speeds up read-heavy applications by serving data from memory instead of a slower backing database.

distractors.B: ElastiCache supports Memcached and Redis, not specifically 'Ehcache'.
distractors.C: An online store for launching pre-configured software with a few clicks describes AWS Marketplace.
distractors.D: A managed DNS service describes Amazon Route 53, not ElastiCache.

explanation.concept: Organizations centralizes management of many accounts under one management account
explanation.correct: AWS Organizations lets you create and centrally manage a group of AWS accounts from a single management (formerly 'master') account, including consolidated billing and policy enforcement.

distractors.A: AWS WAF filters web traffic to protect applications; it has no multi-account management role.
distractors.B: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations for one account; it doesn't manage multiple accounts.
distractors.D: AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance within an account, not multi-account management.

explanation.concept: Dedicated Hosts expose the physical sockets and cores that most BYOL licensing requires
explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts give you a physical server dedicated to your account with visibility into sockets and physical cores, which is what most existing per-socket or per-core software licenses require — making them the best fit for BYOL.

distractors.A: Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to you but without the host-level visibility (sockets and cores) many BYOL licenses need.
distractors.C: On-Demand instances share underlying hardware among customers and don't expose the physical details BYOL licensing typically requires.
distractors.D: Reserved Instances are a billing discount on shared hardware, not a way to see or control the physical host for licensing.

explanation.concept: Cloud trades capital expenditure for variable operating expenditure
explanation.correct: Moving to AWS replaces large upfront investments in data-center hardware (CapEx) with pay-as-you-go operating expenses, a core financial benefit of cloud computing.

distractors.A: Basic Support is included free for every account, but Business and Enterprise support plans are paid — support isn't free for all customers.
distractors.B: AWS provides tools for data protection, but protection isn't automatic without the customer configuring it.
distractors.D: AWS never takes over responsibility for the customer's applications — that stays with the customer under the shared responsibility model.

explanation.concept: Automate and eliminate single points of failure are core Well-Architected design principles
explanation.correct: Automating wherever possible (D) and removing single points of failure (E) are both explicit AWS design principles that make architectures more reliable and easier to evolve.

distractors.A: Global services should be used only where appropriate (e.g., IAM, Route 53); most workloads run in Regional services, so this is not a general rule.
distractors.B: Pay-as-you-go is a pricing model benefit, not itself an architectural design principle.
distractors.C: Treating servers as disposable, replaceable resources — not fixed — is the cloud-native design principle.

explanation.concept: Direct Connect is a dedicated private network link into AWS
explanation.correct: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated, private network connection from your data center to AWS, bypassing the public internet for more consistent latency and bandwidth.

distractors.B: CloudFront is a content delivery network for caching and distributing content, not a private network link.
distractors.C: AWS Snowball is a physical data-transfer device, not a persistent network connection.
distractors.D: Route 53 is DNS; it resolves names, it doesn't create a private network connection.

explanation.concept: VPC provides isolated, per-project network boundaries
explanation.correct: A Virtual Private Cloud lets you define an isolated network with its own IP range, subnets, and routing, so two projects needing different network configurations can each get their own VPC.

distractors.A: Internet gateways connect a VPC to the internet; they don't provide isolation between separate projects.
distractors.C: Security Groups filter traffic to instances within a network; they don't create separate isolated networks.
distractors.D: CloudFront is a content delivery service, unrelated to network isolation.

explanation.concept: WAF filters web requests against common exploits like SQL injection
explanation.correct: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that inspects HTTP(S) requests and blocks patterns matching common exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting, protecting the application layer.

distractors.A: Amazon Cognito handles user sign-up and sign-in and identity federation, not request-level attack filtering.
distractors.B: AWS IAM manages permissions for AWS resources and API calls, not web application traffic inspection.
distractors.C: Aurora is a relational database engine; it doesn't filter or inspect incoming web requests.

explanation.concept: EMR runs big-data processing frameworks (Hadoop/Spark) at scale
explanation.correct: Amazon EMR is a managed big-data platform that runs frameworks like Apache Spark and Hadoop to process and analyze very large data sets.

distractors.B: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker (ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ), not a big-data analytics engine.
distractors.C: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub notification service, unrelated to large-scale data processing.
distractors.D: Amazon SQS is a message queue; it moves messages, it doesn't analyze data sets.

explanation.concept: Hardware and hypervisor layer are AWS's exclusive responsibility
explanation.correct: Creating hypervisors (C) and hardware maintenance (E) happen entirely within AWS's physical infrastructure layer, which only AWS can access and manage — customers have no role in either.

distractors.A: CloudWatch and VPC Flow Logs give the customer visibility into their own resources' network performance, so this is something the customer does, not AWS alone.
distractors.B: Installing software on EC2 instances is the customer's responsibility, since AWS only manages up to the underlying host and hypervisor.
distractors.D: Configuring ACLs (network access rules for a VPC) is a customer configuration task.

explanation.concept: EC2 gives OS-level IaaS control; managed services trade control for less admin burden
explanation.correct: Amazon EC2 is Infrastructure-as-a-Service — you get root or administrator access to the guest OS and can install and configure anything, giving the highest level of control among these options.

distractors.A: Redshift is a managed data warehouse; AWS manages the underlying infrastructure, limiting customer control.
distractors.B: DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database with no server access at all.
distractors.D: RDS manages the underlying database engine and OS for you, trading control for reduced administration.

explanation.concept: Console sign-in uses a username and password by default
explanation.correct: The default credential for signing in to the AWS Management Console as an IAM user is a user name and password; MFA and access keys are additional or alternate mechanisms, not the default console requirement.

distractors.A: MFA is an optional additional factor layered on top of the username and password, not the default credential itself.
distractors.B: Security tokens are temporary credentials (e.g., from STS), not the default IAM user sign-in method.
distractors.D: Access keys authenticate programmatic (API/CLI) access, not console sign-in.

explanation.concept: An AMI is the reusable template for launching identical EC2 instances
explanation.correct: An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) packages the OS, configuration, and software needed to launch an EC2 instance, letting you create as many identical virtual servers from it as you need — the cloud equivalent of an on-premises server template.

distractors.A: IAM manages users and permissions; it has no role in defining server templates.
distractors.B: An internet gateway connects a VPC to the internet; it's unrelated to instance templates.
distractors.C: An EBS snapshot is a point-in-time backup of a volume's data, not a full instance launch template.

explanation.concept: Cloud removes single points of failure and spreads infrastructure across facilities, unlike a single data center
explanation.correct: Eliminating single points of failure (B) is easier in the cloud thanks to multiple AZs and Regions, and AWS's distributed infrastructure (C) spans many facilities globally — both are advantages over a traditional single data center.

distractors.A: Reserved Instances do exist in AWS, but they're a billing commitment, not an advantage over a data center — the cloud advantage is elastic, on-demand capacity, not reserved capacity.
distractors.D: Virtualization exists on-premises too; it isn't unique to the cloud, so it's not a distinguishing advantage.
distractors.E: Dedicated hosting mirrors traditional single-tenant data centers; it isn't a cloud-specific advantage.

explanation.concept: AWS owns hardware patching and the global physical infrastructure
explanation.correct: Hardware patching (D) of the underlying infrastructure and securing the global physical infrastructure (E) — data centers, network backbone — are entirely AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model.

distractors.A: Encrypting EBS volumes is a customer-configured setting, even though AWS provides the encryption capability.
distractors.B: VPC security (route tables, security groups, NACLs) is configured and managed by the customer.
distractors.C: Access permissions (IAM policies) are defined and managed by the customer, not AWS.

explanation.concept: Operational Excellence means monitoring systems and continuously improving processes
explanation.correct: The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value, and continually improving supporting processes and procedures.

distractors.A: Graceful recovery from failure describes the Reliability pillar.
distractors.B: Efficient use of computing resources describes the Performance Efficiency pillar.
distractors.D: Managing data-center operations isn't a Well-Architected pillar concept — AWS manages the data centers, not the customer.

explanation.concept: Edge locations cache and deliver content; they don't load-balance across instances
explanation.correct: Distributing traffic across multiple instances to reduce latency describes load balancing, not what CloudFront edge locations do — edge locations cache and deliver content close to users, so this is the false statement and the correct answer.

distractors.A: True: edge locations do cache recent CloudFront responses close to users.
distractors.B: True: CloudFront edge locations can also accelerate uploads to the origin via optimized routing.
distractors.D: True: distributing content to global users with low latency is exactly CloudFront's purpose.

explanation.concept: CloudTrail logs API activity; Config tracks and evaluates resource configuration changes
explanation.correct: AWS CloudTrail (A) records every API call for auditing 'who did what', and AWS Config (E) tracks resource configuration changes over time and evaluates them against desired rules — together these are the change-management and audit tools.

distractors.B: Amazon Comprehend is a natural-language-processing AI service, unrelated to change tracking.
distractors.C: AWS Transit Gateway is a networking hub for connecting VPCs and on-premises networks, not an audit tool.
distractors.D: AWS X-Ray traces application requests for debugging performance issues, not resource configuration changes.

explanation.concept: ECS orchestrates containers on a cluster of EC2 instances (or Fargate)
explanation.correct: Amazon ECS (Elastic Container Service) runs and manages containerized applications across a cluster of EC2 instances (or serverless Fargate capacity).

distractors.B: AWS Data Pipeline orchestrates data movement and transformation jobs, not container orchestration.
distractors.C: AWS Cloud9 is a cloud-based IDE for writing and debugging code, not a container runtime.
distractors.D: AWS Personal Health Dashboard reports on events affecting your AWS resources, unrelated to running containers.

explanation.concept: CloudTrail's audit log underpins compliance verification
explanation.correct: AWS CloudTrail logs account activity and API calls, providing the audit trail businesses need to demonstrate and verify compliance with internal and regulatory requirements.

distractors.A: CloudFront is a content delivery network; it doesn't provide an activity audit trail for compliance.
distractors.B: CloudEndure Migration replicates servers for migration and disaster recovery, unrelated to compliance auditing.
distractors.C: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs for operational performance, not an audit log of account actions.

explanation.concept: Matching storage class to access pattern is the main lever for S3 cost
explanation.correct: Using the right combination of S3 storage classes (Standard, IA, Glacier, Intelligent-Tiering) based on how frequently each data set is actually accessed is the core way to reduce S3 storage costs.

distractors.A: There's no 'Import/Export' feature that auto-moves files to Glacier — that's done via S3 Lifecycle policies.
distractors.C: S3 buckets are created in a Region, not an Availability Zone, so there is no AZ selection to make that would affect cost.
distractors.D: Moving data from S3 to EBS would increase cost and complexity — EBS is more expensive, per-instance block storage, not a cost-saving move.

explanation.concept: Auto Scaling plus load balancing keeps an architecture available despite failures or demand changes
explanation.correct: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling (B) automatically replaces unhealthy instances and adjusts capacity, and an Elastic Load Balancer (C) routes traffic only to healthy instances — together they maintain availability and fault tolerance.

distractors.A: Direct Connect provides a dedicated network link to AWS; it doesn't add redundancy or fault tolerance to the application itself.
distractors.D: CloudFormation automates resource provisioning (infrastructure as code); it doesn't itself detect failures or reroute traffic.
distractors.E: Network ACLs are stateless traffic filters for a subnet; they don't provide availability or fault tolerance.

explanation.concept: Auto Scaling avoids paying for idle capacity
explanation.correct: Enabling EC2 Auto Scaling means you only run (and pay for) the capacity actually needed at any moment, scaling down during low demand — directly reducing monthly costs.

distractors.B: NLB is a layer-4 load balancer (ALB is the layer-7 choice for HTTP traffic), and either way adding a load balancer adds cost rather than reducing it.
distractors.C: Removing Cost Allocation Tags removes your ability to track and analyze spend — it doesn't reduce actual costs.
distractors.D: Deploying across multiple AZs improves availability but adds cost (more resources running); it doesn't reduce spend.

explanation.concept: Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations to S3
explanation.correct: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses CloudFront's globally distributed edge locations as entry points, routing uploads over optimized AWS backbone network paths to speed up transfers into S3.

distractors.B: AWS WAF filters malicious web traffic; it has nothing to do with upload speed.
distractors.C: Snowmobile is a physical exabyte-scale data-transfer service (a shipping container), not an edge-location-based speed feature.
distractors.D: Snowball is a physical device for bulk offline data transfer, not an edge-location acceleration feature.

explanation.concept: Security Groups are stateful, instance-level firewalls
explanation.correct: Security Groups act as a virtual firewall attached directly to an EC2 instance's network interface, filtering inbound (and outbound) traffic at the instance level.

distractors.A: AWS X-Ray traces requests through an application for debugging and performance analysis, not traffic filtering.
distractors.B: Network ACLs filter traffic at the subnet level, not attached to a specific instance.
distractors.D: VPC Flow Logs capture records of network traffic for analysis; they don't filter or block traffic.

explanation.concept: Global Accelerator optimizes network routing; CloudFront caches content at the edge
explanation.correct: AWS Global Accelerator (B) routes traffic over AWS's global network backbone to the optimal endpoint, and Amazon CloudFront (E) caches content at edge locations near users — both reduce latency for a global application's users.

distractors.A: AWS KMS manages encryption keys; it has no effect on network latency or performance.
distractors.C: Direct Connect provides a dedicated link from a specific on-premises location to AWS, not a general latency-reduction solution for global end users.
distractors.D: AWS Glue is a data integration and ETL service, unrelated to application latency for end users.

explanation.concept: With RDS, the customer owns the schema and data-level settings; AWS owns the engine software and OS
explanation.correct: Building the relational database schema (A) and managing database settings and parameters (C) are customer tasks — RDS is managed, but the data model and tunable settings are still the customer's to design and configure.

distractors.B: RDS performs automated backups for you; that shifts from the customer's responsibility to AWS's.
distractors.D: AWS patches the underlying database engine software for RDS as part of the managed service.
distractors.E: Installing the database software is handled by AWS when you provision an RDS instance — you don't install the engine yourself.

explanation.concept: Structured, relational data maps to RDS
explanation.correct: Structured data with defined schemas and relationships fits a relational database, and Amazon RDS is AWS's managed relational database service (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and others), making it the appropriate migration target.

distractors.A: DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value/document database, better suited to unstructured or flexible-schema data, not this structured relational use case.
distractors.B: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub notification service, not a database.
distractors.D: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, not durable primary storage for structured business data.

explanation.concept: APN Consulting Partners are third-party firms that help customers build and improve on AWS
explanation.correct: AWS Partner Network (APN) Consulting Partners are professional-services firms that help customers design, migrate, and optimize their architectures on AWS — matching a company offering architecture-improvement help.

distractors.B: An AWS Technical Account Manager (TAM) is an AWS employee providing guidance to a single Enterprise Support customer, not a separate consulting company.
distractors.C: APN Technology Partners provide software products (ISV solutions) built on AWS, not architecture consulting services.
distractors.D: AWS Professional Services is AWS's own in-house consulting organization, not a third-party partner program.

explanation.concept: Lambda runs code without provisioning or managing servers
explanation.correct: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that runs your code in response to events without you provisioning, patching, or managing any servers — zero administrative burden for the compute layer.

distractors.A: Amazon Lightsail provides simplified virtual private servers; you still manage an OS instance, unlike serverless Lambda.
distractors.C: RDS instances still require you to manage database settings and instance sizing; it's a managed service but not serverless compute.
distractors.D: EC2 instances are virtual servers you must provision, patch, and manage — the opposite of serverless.

explanation.concept: Fault tolerance means the system keeps working even when components fail
explanation.correct: Because three of six instances crashed with zero customer impact, the architecture tolerated the failure and kept serving traffic — the definition of a fault-tolerant system.

distractors.A: Elasticity is about automatically adjusting capacity up or down with demand, not surviving component failure without impact.
distractors.C: Nothing in the scenario involves data encryption; encryption wasn't demonstrated here.
distractors.D: Scalability is about handling increased load, not about tolerating instance failures without customer impact.
